title: design-kb: content conventions
description: Rules for what content must DO regardless of which component realises it — sibling to design-kb.activity-patterns.json in shape (kbVersion + a flat array of typed entries, additionalProperties false throughout), not an extension of it: activity-patterns answers 'which component realises this', these entries answer 'what must the content do regardless of component'. Opened 14 Sep 2026 with Phase 4 cluster 2's six content-convention rulings (A12, A37, A30, A32, A31, A13); scope is not limited to that cluster — later Phase 4 clusters (knowledge-check spec, summative, terminology, generation defects) land here too, so scope.kind distinguishes role-bound conventions from cross-cutting ones that name no single role.

action.description: Traceability to the action row this entry rules on, in docs/project/audit-2026-09/audit-actions-arising.md.

status.description: Verbatim vocabulary from audit-actions-arising.md line 10, reused rather than a parallel enum so the two files never drift into two different status languages for the same fact.

scope.description: What this convention governs. kind=role for entries bound to one of the twelve content roles (cluster 2's six all are); kind=cross-cutting for future entries that name no single role (e.g. a terminology convention spanning every role). NB for the next author: kind=cross-cutting has no instance yet — all six entries this store opened with (14 Sep 2026) are kind=role. The cross-cutting shape is provided ahead of need for the clusters it is named for (knowledge-check spec, summative, terminology, generation defects), not proven by any real entry; treat it as designed-for, not tested, until the first cross-cutting entry lands.

role.description: Required when kind=role. Same twelve-role enum as design-kb.skeletons.json (duplicated inline rather than cross-file $ref, matching that schema's own convention of repeating the enum at each point of use rather than centralising it).

topic.description: Required when kind=cross-cutting. Free-text naming what the convention spans, e.g. terminology, generation-defects.

unit.description: The structural unit the convention attaches to. Defaults to block; A30 is the first entry that must attach at section level (the rule holds across the section's blocks jointly, not on any one block in isolation).

name.description: Short title, e.g. Concept-group heading convention.

namedPattern.description: Optional: a named pattern this convention establishes or references, e.g. diagnostic-concept (A37). Distinct from activity-patterns/* ids — this names a content-shape pattern, not a component realisation.

rulings.description: The ruling text, ordered. Several actions carry numbered sub-rulings (e.g. A12's three, A13's two); each is its own array item, in the order ruled.

calibratingCase.description: A concrete case the rule cannot be honestly stated without, per A12's own ruling (a substantive-restatement test needs a case that distinguishes it from literal-identity, not a one-line fact). Optional — only used where the ruling itself requires a calibrating example to be legible.

dependsOn.description: Action ids this ruling depends on and cannot be read independently of, e.g. A30 depends on A37 and A55.

amends.description: Docs this ruling supersedes or amends without editing them this sitting — the entry records the supersession, the doc itself is edited later. Precedent: design-kb.skeletons.json's wrapper-close archetype notes, which record superseding open-decisions.md content without editing that file in the same sitting.

leftOpen.description: Questions the ruling explicitly declines to settle, stated so a reader does not mistake silence for an oversight.

records.description: Standalone correction notes carried by the ruling that are not themselves rulings, e.g. A32's eight-vs-twelve-role taxonomy correction, A13's note that AWM has zero forward moves.

sourcePointer.description: Points at the action's own row in audit-actions-arising.md — the durable, repo-tracked record of the ruling — never at ephemeral working files outside the repo.
